newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia should rely less on MidEast oil after US-Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Asia should rely less on MidEast oil after US-Iraq.

text.p: The latest U.S.-Iraq tensions highlight the need for Asian oil consumers to be less dependent on Middle East crude, a Japanese exploration company official said on Wednesday.
"It is essential to increase the self-sufficiency of oil and gas for the sake of energy security in our region." saidAkira Sakurai, Vice President of Japan National Oil Corporation (JNOC).
"We should strive to promote and accelerate the exploration and development activities," he told a regional offshore oil conference.
Sakurai said consuming countries needed to understand the seriousness of being over-dependent on Middle East oil due to that region's political volatility.
He said projections by Japan's Institute of Energy Economics put Asia's oil demand at 17.6 million barrrels per day (bpd) in 2000, rising to 20.7 million bpd by 2005.

He said China would be a bigger oil consumer than Japan by 2010, while countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), would use almost the same amount as Japan. ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam
Most Asian countries would become increasingly dependent on imported oil over the next 15 years, he said. Japan now imports nearly 80 percent of its oil from the Middle East.
By 2010, more than 70 percent of Asia's oil requirements would come from the Middle East if current trends continued, Sakurai said.

He said the use of advanced technology would speed up oil and gas exploration in Asia. Such investments should be done by private companies, while governement should provide "reasonably attractive terms and conditions", he added.
JNOC is active in oil exploration and production projects in China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Burma, Pakistan and Papua New Guinea.
